messages.author: ac38d0c8b0675839
messages.subject: spatially explicit Structural Equation Models
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

I am just writing to ask if any you know of any spatially explicit SEM examples (i.e. SEM that can deal spatial autocorrelation) implemented with lavaan? Apologies for the vague request, but I have already investigated this topic quite a bit and I have discovered for myself that there are many ways of addressing the spatial autocorrelation problem. I have some gridded data so, my spatial variables are in the format of coordinates and I have come to the conclusion that any approaches proposed for areal data would be unsuitable. I have read that one way of dealing with spatial autocorrelation is to use latent variables or to use a spatial weights matrix. The paper of reference where I have found this is: "Folmer, Henk, and Johan Oud. "How to get rid of W: a latent variables approach to modelling spatially lagged variables. Environment and planning. A 40.10 (2008): 2526". I was wondering whether there is a lavaan implementation of this? Or in general, are there any references that you recommend does anyone have some code snippets?

thanks in advance for your help,

Simone

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: spatially explicit Structural Equation Models
parts:
Lavaan or most popular SEM packages cannot implement spatial SEM. See Chapter 39 in 

http://www.guilford.com/books/Handbook-of-Structural-Equation-Modeling/Rick-Hoyle/9781462516797/contents

I think she used Bayesian approach to run spatial SEM.

messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: Re: spatially explicit Structural Equation Models
parts:
So, there was just a paper on spatially explicit SEM in Ecology:
http://www.esajournals.org/doi/abs/10.1890/13-1997.1

The paper includes code that uses lavaan as a base.  Perhaps it would be worth seeing if some of this could be rolled into either lavaan or an accompanying library.

Here’s the code and data (freely available):
http://www.esapubs.org/archive/ecol/E095/216/suppl-1.php

I’m also cc-ing one of the study’s authors who might have further answers.

-Jarrett
